record.context_brief: whether Fourier magnitudes determine degree below the known regularity threshold
record.original_question: Let f,g: S^1 -> S^1 have Fourier coefficients a_n(f) and a_n(g) with |a_n(f)| = |a_n(g)| for every n in Z. Theorem 5.5 says deg f = deg g for f,g in W^{1/3,3}(S^1;S^1), hence also for Holder maps of exponent alpha > 1/3. Does the same conclusion hold when f,g are in W^{1/p,p}(S^1;S^1) for p > 3, or when f,g are in C^{0,alpha}(S^1;S^1) for alpha <= 1/3?

artifact.category_tag: Fractional Sobolev maps to the circle
artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a measurable map $h:S^1\to\mathbb{C}$, denote by $a_n(h)=\frac{1}{2\pi}\int_{S^1} h(e^{i\theta})e^{-in\theta}\,d\theta$, $n\in\mathbb{Z}$, its Fourier coefficients. For $s\in(0,1)$ and $p\in[1,\infty)$, the fractional Sobolev space $W^{s,p}(S^1;S^1)$ consists of measurable maps $f:S^1\to S^1$ with
$$\iint_{S^1\times S^1}\frac{|f(x)-f(y)|^p}{|x-y|^{1+sp}}\,dx\,dy<\infty.$$
For such $f$ the topological degree $\deg f\in\mathbb{Z}$ is well defined whenever $sp\ge 1$, in particular in $W^{1/p,p}(S^1;S^1)$ for every $p\ge 1$. The space $C^{0,\alpha}(S^1;S^1)$ ($0<\alpha\le 1$) consists of Hölder continuous maps $f:S^1\to S^1$ of exponent $\alpha$; for $\alpha>0$ the degree is also defined.

It is known that if $f,g\in W^{1/3,3}(S^1;S^1)$ satisfy $|a_n(f)|=|a_n(g)|$ for every $n\in\mathbb{Z}$, then $\deg f=\deg g$; consequently the same conclusion holds for $f,g\in C^{0,\alpha}(S^1;S^1)$ with $\alpha>1/3$.

Question: Does the conclusion $\deg f=\deg g$ continue to hold under the hypothesis $|a_n(f)|=|a_n(g)|$ for all $n\in\mathbb{Z}$ when:
(a) $f,g\in W^{1/p,p}(S^1;S^1)$ for some $p>3$; or
(b) $f,g\in C^{0,\alpha}(S^1;S^1)$ for some $\alpha\le 1/3$?
